provenance.headline: MECHANICS ARE OFFICIAL, BADGES CORROBORATED, AND 35 ATTRIBUTE CAPS ARE PROVEN BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES THAT AGREE. The build-point budget is now known to be the WRONG SHAPE: 2K27 asks you to fill to 99 Overall.
explanation: OFFICIAL (from https://nba.2k.com/2k27/features/myplayer-builder/):
- 53 badges (matches this dataset exactly), across six disciplines.
- 20 badge slots per build, all available immediately; TOKENS are what you must earn to fill them.
- Badge tokens are earned by PLAYING — discipline meters, Team Practice drills, Gatorade workouts —
NOT by attribute allocation. Reassignable, but in-game tokens stay locked to their discipline.
- Badge token cost VARIES BY SIZE AND POSITION: 'taller players may see a different number of
tokens required than shorter ones for the same Badge'.
- LEGEND badges cannot be obtained at build creation. They are reached through Synergy.
- SYNERGY: 16 slots, twelve +1 and four +2. A Fused badge also refunds its badge tokens.
- 5 Takeover slots; 24 Takeover Abilities of which 19 are unlockable; 15 Takeover Perks.
- Cap Breaker preview unlocks once the build reaches 99 OVR in the Builder.
- Builder paths: Create Your Own, Community Builds, and 40 Signature Blueprints.
READ OFF THE REAL BUILDER (NBA 2K HQ app) — three builds:
- PF 6'11"/210/6'11" (BUCKET CHASER), SG 6'8"/190/6'8" (2-WAY PLAYMAKING CREATOR) and
SG 6'5"/200/6'8" (2-WAY OFF-SCREEN SHOOTER), with their full Cap Breaker tables.
- 35 attribute caps PROVEN, by two independent routes that AGREE where they overlap:
'builder-max' — the slider screen prints 'current / MAX' beside each attribute;
'ladder-lock' — a cap breaker ladder ending in a LOCKED slot has reached the ceiling.
Three-Point on the 6'5" frame is 93 by both. That agreement is what licenses the ladder rule
everywhere else. A ladder that spends all five slots without locking gives a lower bound only.
- The derived caps are coherent across frames: Three-Point 93/92/91 and Perimeter Defense 96/87/77
fall with height, Block 67/75/>=90 rises, Steal runs 99/84/67.
- The linear model, scored against those 35: 6.3 mean absolute error, high on 24 of 35.
- THE BUDGET MECHANIC: the builder shows an OVR meter and 'Fill to a 99 Overall to Continue'. There
is no point pool. The real constraint is OVR(attributes) = 99, and the cost of a point is that
attribute's weight in the per-position OVR formula. Those weights are NOT published, so the app
still uses an invented point pool of the same shape. See budget.json -> actualMechanic.
- The builder also shows a token count per discipline AT BUILD CREATION that tracks the allocation
(19 Shooting / 5 Playmaking on the 6'5" build). This tensions with 2K's 'tokens are earned by
playing'; both may hold. Recorded in badge-tokens.json -> observedAtBuildCreation, not acted on.
SOURCED + CORROBORATED:
- All 53 badges' requirements, AND/OR logic and HEIGHT RANGES from NBA 2K Lab, cross-checked
against a second independent chart: 211 of 212 tiers agree. Run: npm run data:crosscheck
- Badge TOKEN COSTS for 42 of 53 badges, from the 2K27 badge cost charts. Note these are a
SINGLE-BODY SNAPSHOT — 2K says cost varies by size, so they are only exact at one height.
- Animation and takeover thresholds from a community 'best value thresholds' sheet.
NOT SOURCED (assume wrong): attribute CAP magnitudes on any frame with no transcribed build, the
per-position OVR WEIGHTS that are the real budget, per-point COST CURVES, the size of the token pool
at any progression level, the per-discipline slot split, the height/position token cost adjustment,
and HOW MANY cap breakers a player may claim (the per-slot GAINS are verified; the budget is not).
KNOWN GAPS: 15 of the 19 unlockable Takeover Abilities have no known requirements and are absent.
Token costs for the 11 Rebounding/Physicals badges are inferred from the pattern of the other 42.
provenance.howToReplace: See docs/DATA.md. Replace values in place and set each record's verification.status with a source. Nothing in the UI or engine hard-codes these numbers.

verificationLevels.verified: Confirmed against the shipped NBA 2K27 builder or an official 2K source. Safe to trust.
verificationLevels.community-verified: Taken from the supplied NBA 2K27 badge charts / community threshold sheets. Trust with care; re-check against the NBA 2K HQ app.
verificationLevels.estimated: Derived or interpolated from partially known data, or read off a degraded source image. Directionally useful, numerically approximate.
verificationLevels.deprecated: Known to be wrong / no longer applies. Retained for history, ignored by the engine.

uiWarnings.globalBanner: Mechanics and badge data are sourced. 35 attribute caps across three frames are PROVEN from the NBA 2K HQ app — by the slider screen's max and by cap-breaker lock-out, which agree where they overlap — plus lower bounds on the rest; other frames use a model measured 6.3 points off and biased high. The BUILD POINT BUDGET is the weakest part left: 2K27 actually constrains you to fill to 99 Overall, and the OVR weights are unknown, so treat every 'costs N points' figure as a ranking, not a quantity.

changes: CONFIRMED THE CAP DERIVATION. The builder's attribute slider screen prints 'current / MAX' beside each attribute, which is a cap read directly. On the 6'5" frame it says Three-Point 93/93 — exactly what 0.7.0 derived from that attribute's cap breaker ladder locking at 93. Two independent routes, same number. Every other slider figure is consistent too: Mid-Range max 96 against a derived floor of >=95, Free Throw 99 against >=95, Pass Accuracy 99 against >=75, Ball Handle 95 against >=75. No contradictions.
Added those five direct readings as exact caps, taking the proven total from 31 to 35, and added capEvidence recording which route proved each one.
Model accuracy re-scored against the larger set: 6.3 mean absolute error over 35 caps, high on 24.

THE BUILD POINT BUDGET IS THE WRONG SHAPE, and now demonstrably so. 2K27's builder has no point pool — it shows an Overall meter and 'Fill to a 99 Overall to Continue'. The real constraint is OVR(attributes) = 99, so the cost of an attribute point is its weight in the per-position OVR formula. Those weights are not published anywhere supplied, so the invented pool stays as a same-shaped stand-in, with the real mechanic recorded in budget.json -> actualMechanic. Consequence for readers: every 'costs N points' figure in the app is ORDINAL, not cardinal.

Recorded that the builder shows a badge-token count per discipline AT BUILD CREATION which tracks the allocation (19 Shooting, 5 Playmaking on the 6'5" build). This tensions with 2K's official 'tokens are earned by playing'; a build may start with attribute-derived tokens and earn more later. The current linear-by-investment model fits both counts exactly at freeBelow 64 / pointsPerToken 3 — but that is two parameters on two observations, so nothing was changed. The other four discipline counts from the same build would be a real test.
Added 2K's published build-name vocabulary (45 names). It is explicitly partial: two observed names are absent from it entirely, and a third appears only with a '2-Way' prefix the app did not show.

CORRECTION, and the reason for the version bump. 0.6.0 published 21 numbers as verified caps for PF|83|210|83. They were not caps — they were what that player ALLOCATED. The builder's Cap Breaker page labels its first column 'Original Cap', and I read that as the frame's ceiling. It is the build's current rating.

Two more builds made the error unmissable. Ball Handle reads 70 on a 6'5" guard, 86 on a 6'8" guard and 75 on a 6'11" big; Pass Accuracy reads 65 / 87 / 77; Speed With Ball 73 / 80 / 68. No body-cap model makes a 6'5" guard the worst ball handler of the three. Those columns track the ARCHETYPE — the 6'8" is a Playmaking Creator, the 6'5" an Off-Screen Shooter who never dribbles.

WHAT ACTUALLY EXPOSES A CAP is the padlock. A cap breaker ladder that ends in a LOCKED slot has run into the frame's ceiling, so that row's New Cap IS the cap. A ladder that spends all five slots without locking merely ran out of slots and gives a lower bound. caps.json now carries `caps` (31 proven) and `capFloors` (32 lower bounds) derived that way.

The derived caps are coherent across frames in a way the raw columns never were: Three-Point 93 / 92 / 91 and Perimeter Defense 96 / 87 / 77 fall with height, Block 67 / 75 / >=90 rises with it, Steal runs 99 / 84 / 67. That coherence is the evidence the derivation is right.
computeCaps now lifts a modelled cap to any proven floor, so the app can never claim a ceiling the builder was observed to exceed. That silently fixed 8 attributes.

Model accuracy re-measured against the corrected caps: 6.6 mean absolute error over 31 proven caps, high on 24. The earlier 12.9 figure was measured against the wrong numbers and is withdrawn. Still not refit.

Cap breaker tables are now keyed by BUILD, not by body, and carry `body` plus `sampledAt` (the allocation the ladder was measured from). The planner applies a row only where the build's rating equals sampledAt, and reports 'allocation-mismatch' rather than extrapolating.

Dropped the 'only place breakers on attributes already at their cap' rule, which was an artefact of the wrong model. Post Control 31 -> 77 on the 6'5" build is a breaker ladder starting nowhere near a ceiling.

The loader now cross-checks the two derivations against each other in both directions: sampledAt + slots must equal newCap, a locked row's newCap must match caps.json's exact cap, and an unlocked row's newCap must match its floor. These are the guards that would have caught the original misreading.
Added the two new official build names, and pointed Two-Way Shot Creator at the 6'8" frame and Lockdown Defender at the 6'5" frame, so three presets now plan against proven ceilings.

FIRST VERIFIED ATTRIBUTE CAPS. All 21 caps for a 6'11" / 210 lb / 6'11" PF, read off the NBA 2K HQ app's builder, are in caps.json -> overrides.entries under PF|83|210|83. Every other body still uses the invented linear model.

Scored the linear cap model against those caps for the first time: mean absolute error 12.9 points, biased HIGH on 19 of 21 attributes, and wrong in SIGN on shooting for a slender big (it predicts 86/84 mid-range/three where the builder gives 94/91). Recorded in caps.json -> capModel.measuredAccuracy. The model was deliberately NOT refit — four coefficients per attribute fitted to one body would look calibrated without being calibrated.

REWROTE THE CAP BREAKER MODEL, which was wrong in kind rather than degree. It assumed four breakers each worth a flat +1, capped at two per attribute. The builder actually gives every attribute FIVE slots, each worth a different per-attribute amount (+7 on Steal's first slot, +1 on Close Shot's), with gains diminishing down the row and whole attributes locked out entirely.

cap-breakers.json is now a per-body gain table keyed like the cap overrides, with null for a locked slot and a published newCap per row. `totalAvailable`, `maxPerAttribute` and `raisePerBreaker` are gone.
A body with no transcribed table now gets NO cap breaker plan rather than a guessed one, and the UI says so.

The one thing the screenshots do not settle is how many breakers a player may claim. Recorded as an explicit unknown with two documented readings; the app defaults to the conservative 'shared pool of 5' rather than the reading that would hand this frame +112 attribute points.

planCapBreakers now allocates RUNS of slots, not one slot at a time. Pass Accuracy's slots are +2 each and no single one crosses a threshold, but three together cross four of them; the old one-slot-lookahead greedy saw zero gain and left every breaker unplaced.
The loader now cross-checks the two transcriptions against each other: original cap + slot gains must equal the published newCap, and an unlocked slot may not follow a locked one.
Recorded BUCKET CHASER, the first confirmed official 2K27 build name, in archetypes.json -> officialBuildNames.

Retargeted the Stretch Big preset onto the transcribed frame, so at least one preset plans against real ceilings. Its soft targets were rebuilt from thresholds that are actually reachable there — the old ones (Block 84, Defensive Rebound 87) sat above the real caps of 70 and 80.

Corrected the badge token model against 2K's official page: tokens are earned by PLAYING, not derived from attribute allocation. The old linear-by-investment default was simply the wrong model; default is now a flat per-discipline pool you set to your own progress.
Re-added the LEGEND badge tier. 2K states it exists but cannot be obtained at build creation — it is reached only through Synergy, so it carries no attribute requirement row.
Replaced the invented badge-boost numbers with the official Synergy system: 16 slots, twelve +1 and four +2 (was 2 and 1).
Modelled that a Fused badge refunds the tokens spent equipping it.
Takeover slots corrected from primary/secondary to the official 5; recorded that 24 abilities exist and 19 are unlockable, of which only 4 have known requirements here.
Added Hydration Hero, officially named, with no published attribute requirement.
Added a costByBody model: 2K says badge token cost varies with size and position, so the chart costs are now explicitly a single-body snapshot with an adjustment hook, defaulted to zero.
Confirmed against 2K: 53 badges, 20 badge slots, six disciplines, and the 99-OVR cap breaker preview.
Added data/2k27/sources/ for independently-produced sources, and a cross-check that diffs the shipped dataset against each one.
Transcribed the @jpforthreee badge requirements chart as a second source: 211 of 212 tiers and height gates agree with the NBA 2K Lab import.
The one disagreement (Smooth Operator max height 6'11" vs unrestricted) is recorded as a known conflict, shown in the UI, and left unresolved rather than silently decided.
npm run data:crosscheck exits non-zero on any disagreement not recorded with a note, so a conflict can be accepted but not ignored.
Imported all 53 badges from NBA 2K Lab: requirements, AND/OR logic and per-badge HEIGHT RANGES.
Added the missing Rebounding badges (Boxout Boss, Breaker, Crasher, Possession Closer, Sync Snatcher) and Physicals badges (Brick Wall, Bruiser, Flash, Pogo Stick, Slippery Off-Ball, Work Horse).
Removed Rebound Chaser, which I had reconstructed from a single line of the best-value sheet and which does not exist on 2K Lab.

Resolved all four rows previously flagged as unreadable from the chart images: Post Fade Phenom Bronze Mid-Range is 60 (not 83, so the ladder is monotonic after all); Pick Dodger, Wall Up and Post Lockdown all had wrong tier values.
Mini Marksman gained its real attribute requirements (Mid-Range or Three-Point 60/79/94/99) — the chart image showed only the height gate.
Badge height gating is now modelled: 25 of 53 badges are height-restricted, so height locks badges out entirely rather than just moving caps.
Corrected the builder height range to 5'9"-7'4", read off 2K Lab's height columns.
Added a documented fallback price for badges with no sourced token cost, flagged as inferred everywhere it is used.
Added scripts/import-2klab.mjs so the badge data can be re-imported when 2K Lab updates.
Replaced all badge data with sourced NBA 2K27 requirements and badge token costs (Shooting, Playmaking, Defense, Finishing).
Removed Stamina: not a 2K27 builder attribute, raised in-game at the Gatorade gym.
Removed Acceleration, added Agility, which is what 2K27 defensive badges actually require.
Split Rebounding out of Defense into its own discipline (2K27 has six badge disciplines).
Dropped the Legend badge tier: 2K27 charts show Bronze/Silver/Gold/Hall of Fame only.
Added badge-tokens.json for the new token + slot economy.
Added support for 'any of' badge requirements, which 2K27 uses heavily.
Corrected the sign of the weight and wingspan effect on Perimeter Defense and Driving Dunk caps.
Rewrote animations and takeovers to only what the best-value threshold sheet names.
Initial scaffold with fully invented placeholder data.

files.describes: Attribute definitions, six disciplines, min/max, cost curve binding.
Per-point upgrade cost curves referenced by attributes. UNSOURCED.
Positions and their body-setting envelopes. UNSOURCED.
Height / weight / wingspan legal ranges. UNSOURCED.
How body settings translate into per-attribute maximums. One body's caps are VERIFIED from the real builder; every other body uses a linear model whose error is measured in capModel.measuredAccuracy.
Badges, tiers, requirements, height ranges and token costs. Requirements SOURCED from 2K Lab; token costs sourced for 42 of 53.
Badge token economy: per-discipline pools and badge slots. Mechanic sourced, quantities not.
Animation packages and their requirements. SOURCED but incomplete.
Takeovers and their unlock requirements. SOURCED but likely incomplete.
Cap breaker gain tables, keyed by body: five slots per attribute, per-attribute variable gains, locked slots. VERIFIED for one body. How many breakers a player may claim is NOT sourced.
Maximum +1 / +2 badge level boost rules. UNSOURCED.
Declared attribute interaction rules. Modelling choices, not game rules.
Named build archetypes plus officialBuildNames, the in-game names observed for specific bodies. Threshold values sourced; archetype names are community convention.
Independently-produced sources the dataset is cross-checked against. Not loaded by the app.
